在數日前推出用戶名預留系統後，WhatsApp 現正開始為少數用戶啟用完整功能。以下是詳情。

WhatsApp Starts Activating Reserved Usernames

WhatsApp Launches Username Reservation System — Here's What You Should Know

You can claim yours by going to Settings > Account > Username, and choose whether you want anyone who knows your username to be able to message you, or whether you'd like new contacts to enter a four-digit PIN in addition to your username.

If the username you choose matches an account already established on another Meta platform like Facebook or Instagram, you may need to prove that you control that account too. This is intended to prevent people from grabbing high-profile usernames and potentially impersonating others in a way that could lead to scams.

That said, WhatsApp is now starting to activate reserved usernames for a small number of accounts, as spotted by WABetaInfo.

Users who are part of this first wave will now see a banner at the top of their chat list letting them know their username is live and ready to be shared with new contacts.

According to the report, the feature is rolling out to both beta testers and users on the stable version of WhatsApp, but emphasizes that it appears to be limited to a "very small number of users" for now.

To check whether your account has access, look for the banner at the top of your chat list, or head to the Username section of your profile settings. There, you'll be notified whether your username is live, or you'll see a message saying: "Usernames are coming soon, you'll be notified when it's ready."
